networkHosts.observed: node-gyp's default dist URL, reached whenever the header cache is cold. NOT observed in the 311-package corpus run: that harness sets `npm_config_nodedir` to the provisioned Node root, as nub does, so node-gyp never fetched. Absence there is not evidence the entry is unnecessary — it is evidence the corpus did not exercise a cold header cache.

networkHosts.artifact: Release-asset tarballs under /<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/ — how most prebuilt native addons and vendor binaries are published
networkHosts.observed: Promoted 2026-07-30 out of notGranted, where it was recorded as `write-capable`. The demand: 17 of the 21 network denials in the three-OS corpus baseline (macOS 33 breaks of 143 admissible, Linux 24 of 143, Windows 13 of 133) are this host — the single largest lever in the run. Verbatim from the denied arm of the Linux corpus run: `FetchError: request to https://github.com/cube-js/cube/releases/download/v1.4.4/native-linux-x64-glibc-fallback.tar.gz failed, reason: getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN github.com`. The refusal this supersedes rested on git-receive-pack sharing the hostname with the release-asset route; it is answered by the jail's identity-based model rather than by new evidence about the host, and the argument is in data/README.md. Two limits worth stating. The requester population is NOT enumerated here — 46 corpus packages fetch this host, 14 of them blocking on the Linux arm — and this entry alone does not unblock them: the two gates compose, so a package must be named in some entry's fetchedBy or in packageNetwork.full AND target an admitted host. And Windows keeps the deny-all regardless, so nothing here reaches it there.

networkHosts.artifact: The bytes of a github.com release asset — the signed, expiring URL a /releases/download/ request redirects to
networkHosts.observed: Measured 2026-07-28 against a real release asset: github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/… 302s here. A load-bearing entry rather than a convenience, on the same pairing as download.cypress.io with cdn.cypress.io — the fetch re-applies this allowlist to EVERY redirect hop, so github.com alone resolves nothing and tree-sitter-cli's artifact went from 0 to 15,599,168 bytes only once this host was reachable too. Deliberately absent alongside it: raw.githubusercontent.com, which github.com/<owner>/<repo>/raw/… redirects to. That is arbitrary repo content rather than a published artifact, and no measured package needs it.

networkHosts.artifact: The same release-asset CDN under its older hostname, still used by directly-published asset URLs
networkHosts.observed: Not the spelling any corpus run hit — the corpus exercised the /releases/download/ route, which 302s to release-assets above. Carried over from nub's own prefetch redirect allowlist (crates/nub-cli/src/pm_engine/build_prefetch.rs), which retains it because a directly-published asset URL still lands on this hostname. Absence from the corpus is not evidence the entry is unnecessary, on the same reading as nodejs.org: the corpus did not exercise the route that reaches it. The fetchedBy names are the packages that fetch the CDN, not packages observed on this spelling.

packageGrants.mechanism: scripts/postinstall.js does three things, and each masks the next: it calls process.chdir(INIT_CWD); createDefaultGeneratedThrowFiles unconditionally mkdirs path.join(__dirname, '../../../.prisma'), a sibling of @prisma in the package's own enclosing node_modules; then it re-execs the prisma CLI as `prisma generate`, which reads the consumer's prisma/ schema directory. The generated client lands inside package_dir and needs no grant.
packageGrants.observed: EPERM mkdir <own node_modules>/.prisma, then EPERM uv_cwd on chdir(INIT_CWD), then EPERM reading the consumer's prisma/ schema. Verified by artifact, not exit code: a generated client of 71282 B carrying a per-run schema nonce, against absent output and 2 EPERMs without the grants. Presence alone is not a valid check here — the script writes throw-stubs before every guard, so it exits 0 having generated nothing.

packageGrants.mechanism: Its postinstall runs `indefinitely-typed`, which computes path.resolve(cwd, '../..'), asserts that directory is named node_modules, then mkdirs @types there and copySyncs each --folder argument into it. The write target is <own node_modules>/@types — the same enclosing-node_modules sibling shape as Prisma, under a different name.
packageGrants.observed: EPERM mkdir <own node_modules>/@types. With the grant, 20 copied type folders present; without it, absent.

packageGrants.mechanism: config/scripts/postinstall.js reads the CONSUMER's package.json for msw.workerDirectory, returns silently if absent, and otherwise re-execs its own CLI with cwd set to INIT_CWD to copy mockServiceWorker.js into each listed directory. The directories come from the field rather than a literal because msw imposes no convention — the consumer picks them.
packageGrants.observed: EPERM uv_cwd. The cwd need bites first: without projectCwd the child dies in uv_cwd before it reads the field at all. With the grants, msw's worker script is present; without them, absent.

notGranted.comment: Documentation only. Nothing in this object is compiled into any allowlist; it records hosts that a real install was measured to need and that were not admitted, so a contributor can see the bar before opening a PR. A build-time check keeps this list and networkHosts disjoint, which is also why a PROMOTED host leaves this list outright rather than staying behind with an amended rationale — the promotion is recorded on its networkHosts entry instead, and here. PROMOTED 2026-07-30: github.com, out of `write-capable`. Its refusal turned on git-receive-pack sharing a hostname with the release-asset route, so a host-level grant could not admit the fetch without admitting the push, and the recorded plan was to wait for path-scoped proxy support. The identity-based model answers that without the proxy work: no catalog entry means no network at all, an entry means the network the review ratified. The write the refusal feared is thus reachable only by a package a pull request already vetted — a decision the entry makes, not one the hostname makes — while the cost of holding the host fell on 17 unrelated packages, the largest single lever in the three-OS baseline. Entries carry the same provenance fields as networkHosts, because an evidenced candidate is what makes a later promotion reviewable.

hosts.requester: @tensorflow/tfjs-node, chromedriver (also puppeteer and taiko on the earlier macOS pass)
hosts.detail: Refused because an attacker can rent a bucket under the same hostname and read back whatever a confined script writes there — the exfiltration criterion, not an integrity one. Held rather than promoted alongside github.com on 2026-07-30, because the objection is a DIFFERENT one and does not fall to the same argument. github.com's refusal was that a host grant cannot separate a fetch from a push; the package entry is what decides who may push, so the host label was not carrying the control. This one is a standing exfiltration sink — admitting it hands every catalogued package a readable drop for whatever it sends — and no reasoning about package identity narrows that, because every such package is already past the identity gate. The route forward is no longer the path-scoped grant this entry used to nominate (see data/README.md, Known gaps): it is a maintainer ruling on whether the two observed prefixes (/tensorflow/ and /chrome-for-testing-public/) being stable and single-tenant is worth the sink, weighed against the packages it breaks — @tensorflow/tfjs-node and the chromedriver family. Open.
hosts.observed: Both artifacts requested in the denied arm of the Linux corpus run; libtensorflow logged as `* Downloading libtensorflow` immediately before the URL.

hosts.detail: A soft fetch that degrades rather than failing does not earn an entry: the CLI reports `failed to install amplify binary` with egress denied, but the install itself still exits 0.
hosts.observed: Error fetching release: getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN package.cli.amplify.aws, followed by `failed to install amplify binary`, in the denied arm of the Linux corpus run.

hosts.detail: Recorded as an evidenced candidate, not as a disqualification: no write-capable route or multi-tenant namespace has been established for it, and the fetch is a dedicated single-tenant vendor binary path. Whether it is admitted is a maintainer call, and it is deliberately left out of networkHosts until then. Note the requester is wrangler 1.x, which prints its own deprecation notice directing users to the `wrangler` package — so the demand may not survive the version it was measured on.
